subject.title: [Feature]: cron jobs.d/ directory support (one file per job, for NixOS/GitOps declarative setups)

question: Should OpenClaw support declarative per-job cron files as an import/reconcile artifact feeding SQLite, as a steady-state jobs.d runtime store, or not in core for now?
rationale: Current code, docs, tests, and repository policy make SQLite the canonical cron runtime store, while the request adds new config/storage behavior with compatibility, identity, deletion, and path-safety implications that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Reconcile Into SQLite
options.body: Add a documented deterministic import/export or reconcile surface for per-job JSON that validates files and writes canonical SQLite rows without making file polling the runtime store.

options.title: Runtime Directory Store
options.body: Add a new jobs.d-backed cron store mode with explicit migration, symlink, path-safety, stable filename, and upgrade semantics owned by maintainers.

options.title: Decline Core Storage Mode
options.body: Keep the supported path as CLI/Gateway API plus external user-side scripts unless stronger demand or a plugin/API gap changes the product direction.

recommendation.title: Reconcile Into SQLite
recommendation.body: Add a documented deterministic import/export or reconcile surface for per-job JSON that validates files and writes canonical SQLite rows without making file polling the runtime store.

likelyOwner.reason: The product decision most directly affects the current cron persistence and SQLite storage boundary introduced in the traced cron persistence work.
